topic: Calcutta HC: a car parking allotment does not automatically pass to the buyer of a flat unless it is expressly conveyed - Section 8, Transfer of Property Act, 1882 examined; 1993 sale deed of Apartment 3A, Golf Green Urban Complex, had no parking in its schedule; Housing Board never conveyed parking space BG-9 to the vendors; side-letter promise gives no claim against the Board; writ against the Board's 19 Sep 2019 memo dismissed (Shrawan Kumar Agarwal v. West Bengal Housing Board, WPA 2129 of 2020, Justice Partha Sarathi Sen, decided 19 Nov 2026, reported 21 Nov 2026)

slides.title: Bought a flat? Parking is **not automatic**
slides.subtitle: A parking space passes to the buyer only if the **sale deed clearly transfers it**.
slides.cite: **Shrawan Kumar Agarwal v. West Bengal Housing Board** · WPA 2129 of 2020 · Justice Partha Sarathi Sen · 19 November 2026

slides.label: What happened
slides.title: A flat sold, **parking promised**
bullets: In **1992**, the earlier owners of a Housing Board flat applied for a parking space and deposited **Rs 7,000**. They got a provisional allotment letter.
On **30 March 1993**, they sold the flat to the petitioner by a registered deed. The deed's schedule did **not mention any parking**.
In a separate letter that day, they promised to hand over the parking **once the Board allotted it** to them.

slides.label: The dispute
slides.title: The buyer **claimed the space**
bullets: In **1997**, the Board decided to allot space **BG-9** to the earlier owner, with a conveyance deed to follow. That deed was **never made**.
In **2019**, the Board revoked its 1997 memo. The buyer challenged this in the High Court.
He relied on **Section 8, Transfer of Property Act**, saying he had stepped into the sellers' shoes, and offered to pay all charges.

slides.label: What the Court said
slides.title: Not part of **what was sold**
bullets: A sale passes the seller's interest in the property and its legal incidents. But the buyer could not show the parking was an **inseparable part** of the flat.
The deed did not include parking, and the Board had **never conveyed** the space to the sellers. If anyone was wronged, it was the **sellers**, not the buyer.
The writ petition was **dismissed**, and the earlier interim order was vacated.
slides.note: **Law fact:** A private letter from the seller is not a claim against the allotting authority. What counts is **what the registered deed transfers**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Read your **sale deed** carefully
bullets: This ruling turns on its own facts. It does **not** say flat buyers can never get parking.
If parking matters to you, check that the **deed itself** clearly lists it, not just a side promise.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Bought a flat and assumed the parking space came with it? Not unless your sale deed says so, says the Calcutta High Court 🚗🏢

In 1992, the earlier owners of a West Bengal Housing Board flat applied for a parking space and deposited Rs 7,000. In March 1993 they sold the flat by a registered deed that said nothing about parking, but in a separate letter promised to hand over the space once the Board allotted it. The Board decided in 1997 to allot space BG-9 to the earlier owner, but never executed a conveyance, and in 2019 it revoked that decision.

The buyer argued that under Section 8 of the Transfer of Property Act he had stepped into the sellers' shoes. Justice Partha Sarathi Sen disagreed. The buyer could not show that the parking was an inseparable part of the flat or that it was included in the deed, and the Board had never conveyed the space to the sellers in the first place. If anyone was aggrieved, it was the sellers, not the buyer. The writ petition was dismissed.

The lesson for home buyers: a side promise from the seller is not enough. If parking matters to you, make sure the registered deed itself clearly includes it.

Case: Shrawan Kumar Agarwal v. The West Bengal Housing Board & Ors., WPA 2129 of 2020
Court: Calcutta High Court, Justice Partha Sarathi Sen (19 November 2026)
